Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: premium terrain art direction reference 01 for the science fiction exploration game Star Abyss. An actual painted/rendered image for review, not a diagram or UI.
Primary request: one complete spherical starting planet suspended in space, large in frame with all edges visible. Show an organic irregular continent extending mostly west of a dry violet-grey basalt basin, with a hooked southeastern peninsula, irregular eastern coastal inlets and a few fractured offshore islands. This is the geography identity to retain across the entire image series.
Scene: ocean-rich rocky planet with one dominant broad continent and smaller irregular far-side land glimpses; a narrow charcoal bare mountain spine along the northwestern interior; extensive gently undulating lowlands, a dry purple-grey basalt impact basin in the eastern inland, muted sage plains outside it, deep teal forests farther east, a connected branching river draining east through wetlands into one broad estuary and the blue ocean. The basin occupies a modest part of the continent and does not resemble a round or square patch pasted on top. It is dry and has no lake.
Style: polished realistic game environment concept painting, restrained cinematic light, geological credibility, readable large land masses, broad flat plains, unexaggerated spherical relief. Ocean navy with subdued turquoise shelves. Thin atmosphere, minimal clouds leaving geography visible. Space deep indigo with very subtle violet nebula; no extra foreground planets or rings on this planet.
Composition: landscape image, planet near centered occupying 85% of height, eastern coast and main basin on the sunlit front hemisphere; gentle three-quarter globe view, soft terminator at left, topographic texture coherent from continent to ocean. No collage.
Constraints: same planet identity of purple-grey basalt, grey-brown weathered soil, sage plains, deep teal forests, cyan-to-navy water. Land is organically eroded, no rectangular boundaries, no square high-frequency noise patches, no tiled farmland, no texture seams, no cubic planet, no floating terrain slabs. No snow mountains, deserts, cities, characters, spacecraft, labels, grids, numbers, captions or watermark. It is concept art not a measured map, not game screenshot.

Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: terrain art direction for Star Abyss starting planet, premium realistic game environment concept painting. Input image 1 is the established planet geography and palette reference, not a target for local repainting. Derive a detailed new camera view from this SAME world. Keep purple-grey dry basalt, grey-brown soil, subdued sage grass, dark teal broadleaf vegetation, cyan rivers and navy ocean. Natural large-scale landforms and broad traversable lowland surfaces; not a miniature diorama. Soft grazing neutral daylight with a subtle violet atmospheric cast. Ground scenes may show a subtle lavender space sky and very distant small ringed companion as established world sky, never rings around this planet. No new characters, vehicles, buildings, symbols, HUD, text, labels, watermarks. Avoid rectangular patches, straight texture cutoffs, grid fields, checkerboard ecology, artificial tile boundaries, floating flat terrain slabs, snow mountains or deserts. Rocks have coherent geological strata and irregular weathered edges, not repeated cones or cube stacks. This is concept art not a game screenshot or exact terrain-data map.
Primary request: wide ground-level panorama from a low irregular basalt shelf overlooking the original six-kilometre dry lunar basin. Terrain-only environment reference. Foreground weathered purple-grey stratified basalt with sparse loose chips and smooth fine regolith, never uniformly noisy gravel. Spacious gently sloping open central basin floor, low stepped rock shelves on left, broader naturally eroded mesa on right, a shallow asymmetrical impact crater with a broken rim in the mid-distance, layered canyon walls farther back with a broad walkable corridor between them. Terrain relief in tens of metres nearby, distant enclosing ridges fading with distance. Do not put water, river, grass or forest inside the legacy basin. Show realistic wide flat scale with connected ground; restrained realistic materials readable at game distance, only a few close cracks. Camera 2 metres above ground, wide horizontal image, horizon near upper third. No equipment or structures. Basalt region must continue beyond frame and weather naturally at its periphery, not sit on a square platform.

Input image 2 is the approved-for-review basin material and wide ground scale reference. Transform the camera to the dry basin's EASTERN OUTER MARGIN, looking out toward distant plains. One single ultra-wide continuous landscape, camera about 8 metres above ground, low oblique view. At left and foreground purple-grey stratified basalt outcrops taper into loose gravel, then weathered finer grey-brown silt between winding low ridges. Isolated sage grass tufts grow in the fine soil first, merging over kilometres into spacious gently rolling open grassland dominating the middle and far distance. Dry erosion channels subtly guide the ground, no water inside basin, a distant river only on far eastern plains and no ocean visible here. This image is specifically about NATURAL IRREGULAR ECOLOGICAL TRANSITION, not stripes: long uneven tongues of grass run into channels in the basalt while low bare knuckles extend into grassland. No hard dividing line, no repeated bands. Background soft low ridges shelter the distant forest so the whole planet's biomes cannot all be seen at once. Keep flat lowland scale expansive; narrow nearby outcrops occupy small minority of the frame. Show continuous height, soil and vegetation changes in the same terrain surface.

Single wide elevated vista looking lengthwise down a large winding geological canyon. Coherent angled bare mountain ridges rise behind layered violet charcoal cliffs; continuous tilted strata can be followed across the canyon sides, weathered ledges taper into scree slopes then a broad green-grey valley floor. A narrow headwater river runs at the lowest point, tributary gullies enter it from mountain slopes, downstream valley opens and gets gentler. A lower natural shelf along one side allows a believable exploration route without artificial roads, rails or bridges. Foreground cliff edge reveals relief while a spacious middle-distance valley prevents this becoming a wall-filled claustrophobic scene. Camera on a mountainside overlook; deep kilometre-scale distance, no exaggerated impossibly vertical spires. Pale areas are exposed weathered rock, absolutely no snow. No ice, glaciers, lakes, volcanoes or crystals in this current baseline terrain image.

Primary request: immersive ground-level river-valley FOREST on the eastern side of the same continent, about the forest leg of the starting planet exploration route. Tall ancient broadleaf trees with buttressed dark weathered trunks, sculptural branching and irregular layered grey-teal crowns; a few very large old trees give the documented future ancient-grove region identity without magic buildings. Camera 2 metres above a gentle grassy bank, looking diagonally through a naturally open clearing into denser forest. A narrow winding clear blue-grey stream passes on the right through smooth purple-grey basalt stones, and continues visibly around a bend; modest exposed root systems hold the bank. On the left foreground sparse grass and scattered young trees interlock with the deeper wooded area. Understory must remain readable and open enough to walk, damp soil and leaf litter, a few ferns and low reeds near water. Bright soft daylight reaches the ground in broad patches, light mist sits only farther down the valley, no fog wall. Background forest-clad lower slopes subtly reveal same basalt geology, no towering canyon enclosing every scene. The horizon cannot reveal ocean, basin and every biome simultaneously. One large wide scene, no inset panels, no glowing mushrooms, no neon fantasy flowers. Show a distinct believable forest environment rather than the same basin composition with trees added.

Input image 2 provides the same river-valley forest vegetation and river material. Derive its downstream lowland WETLAND. Wide low aerial view from about 90 metres above an expansive very gently sloping floodplain. One clearly readable main sinuous river enters from upper left background, joins two minor tributaries, broadens toward foreground right; attached shallow backwaters and irregular reed beds nest along low inside banks, isolated patches of damp silt and smooth grey-purple pebbles. Water should sit at the lowest continuous level, no waterfalls, terraces, raised water platforms or disconnected blue stripes. Reed islands are irregular with tapered ends aligned to flow, freshwater marsh plants stay shallow while scattered trees stand on slightly higher dry hummocks and denser forest recedes inland. Grassy dry levees remain visibly above water with gradual mud-to-sedge-to-grass sequence. Open horizon and broad flat land, distant low basalt ridges only. This is not a giant lake and not a coastal estuary yet; no visible sea, no straight irrigation canals, no checkerboard patches, no rectangular fields. Readable shorelines at foreground and landscape scale, restrained reflections.

Input image 2 is the upstream wetland reference. Derive the coastal endpoint of the same drainage system, on the irregular EASTERN COAST of image 1. One wide panoramic oblique view from a low coastal bluff, about 150 metres above water, looking east toward ocean. A substantial freshwater river enters from lower left through dark teal riverbank forest and subdued sage wetland, then spreads into a few natural sinuous distributaries with long muddy/sandy shoals before openly joining a broad bay. Show the water connection from river to sea unambiguously with no barrier or abrupt height step. Estuary sediment plume fades gently from grey-green to turquoise shallow shelf and deep navy beyond, thin soft wave lines along outer shore. Coastline curls into a hooked rock headland on the right, its exposed purple-grey basalt strata matching inland geology; low beaches, coves and tidal flats interleave naturally rather than forming a perfect ring. A handful of distant fractured islands extend the headland, and open sea reaches horizon. Broad flatter floodplain in middle ground, coastal cliffs localized on headland rather than an entire tall wall. Readable waterlines, no rectangular patches, no giant lake enclosed by mountains, no dam, no roads.

Single wide aerial landscape, camera around 300 metres, not a full globe. Ocean fills about two-thirds of the composition, dark navy toward a far horizon. At left a rugged coastline recedes and breaks into several irregular elongated basalt islands and small eroded sea stacks that follow an underlying curved geological ridge, emphatically not evenly spaced stepping stones. In foreground one large naturally split rock island has low grass on its upper surface, angular weathered cliff fissures, thin pale mineral/salt crust above the spray line on sheltered flats; no desert dunes and no snow. Turquoise shallow water reveals connected submerged rock shelves surrounding some islands, fading with depth rather than a perfect halo around every island. Ocean wave scale stays believable, white surf localized on exposed rocks, dark deep channels between islands. Broad sky and water communicate long-distance exploration and safe natural landing shelves at rare locations. No magical portals, buildings, ships or floating islands in this image; later-world features are a terrain design proposal only.

There is no collage, no separate regions on tiles. Left half broad low-relief sage grassland with subtle undulating drainage and purple-grey bedrock outcrops. Scattered trees become irregular clusters, the clusters merge into dark teal woodland toward right; grassy fingers and clearings extend well into the woodland, and tree fingers follow damp gullies back into open grassland. A sinuous single river arcs through the lower right with small discontinuous reed fringes only in sheltered shallow banks, clear dry higher bank with trees, fine sediment shoals on inner bends. Small dry gullies feed lower points toward river and must not run uphill over ridges. Bedrock, soil moisture, tree density and grass intermix in organic overlapping patterns, not a uniform perfectly even gradient and not checkerboard camouflage. Maintain flat land at continental scale, low hills only, no enormous cliff or mountain ridge, no ocean, no lake, no isolated square patch, no agricultural fields. Camera angle leaves a sliver of low distant skyline for scale; useful terrain reference with maximum readable ground.

Input image 2 is the ground-level dry basalt basin reference and image 3 its eastern transition reference. Create a new view at approximately 1.6 KILOMETRES ABOVE THAT SAME BASIN looking obliquely east. This is an altitude readability reference, not orbital. Wide landscape image, ground fills 90 percent, a thin far horizon and pale violet sky at top. Show the roughly six-kilometre legacy content area as PART OF a much larger organically weathered geological basin, never bounded by a square. Recognizable grey-violet stepped shelves in west foreground, broken impact crater rim toward middle right, an irregular mesa shoulder to the right and natural canyon gaps continuing toward far ridges; broad smooth dry basin floor remains spacious. Three small impact-crater shapes can appear as restrained ground features, not huge perfect circles. Basin outer geology has branching eroded lobes and long gravel fans extending out; bare rock changes gradually into grey-brown sediment, sparse sage patches then broad plains. The greener land and distant forest appear on eastern horizon, ocean hidden at this altitude. The entire basin floor stays dry. Uniformly attached continuous ground with no lifted slab, no isolated patch, no hard outline, no rectangle, no checkerboard. Critically reduce fine surface noise at this altitude: close regolith grains vanish into coherent smooth material values while macro strata, drainage, impact depressions remain readable. Geological borders need to be fuzzy irregular fans rather than a precisely outlined polygon. Preserve ground view material identity, not a different world.

Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: orbital visual target for Star Abyss, reference 11. Input image 1 is the EXACT GEOGRAPHIC IDENTITY to preserve; input image 2 is the basin ground geology identity, not a texture sticker. Reframe image 1 as a farther-out orbit camera view of the SAME complete planet, full sphere comfortably inside frame, occupying about 68 percent of image height with generous dark violet space around it. Preserve its continent silhouette, northwestern mountain spine, eastern inland grey-violet dry geological province, eastward main river/estuary, southeast hooked peninsula, offshore islands and navy ocean. Do not invent a new continent shape, mirror or rotate the continent, or move the basin to a coast. The original six-kilometre gameplay basin is only a SMALL CORE within that larger dry geological province, its actual content boundary must be totally invisible; the broader dry province fades in irregular erosional lobes into sage plains and teal forest. At orbital distance replace all regolith grain and high-frequency materials by integrated broad smooth geological tones; ridges still read in subtle lighting, no gritty speckled island of high detail. A clean gently lit spherical silhouette, thin blue-violet atmosphere, very sparse clouds, soft day/night terminator at left. Planet is truly round rather than a flat disk, with restrained relief silhouette; space behind subtle purple nebula and sparse stars. No spacecraft, astronaut, companion planet, HUD, labels, grids, diagram, border or text. No square, rectangular or diamond-shaped terrain patch; no seams, no checkerboard, no floating land plate, no artificial black hole in surface. No new polar ice cap, snow mountains or deserts. Polished realistic cinematic orbital environment concept, not game screenshot.

Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: large four-view terrain reference sheet for documented but not yet adopted special regions of the SAME Star Abyss starting planet. Input image 1 is the common planet identity and palette. Input image 2 is the basalt geology reference. These are four geographically separate proposals, never four adjoining colored zones. Create a clean 2 by 2 sheet of FOUR LARGE WIDE landscape paintings, each with enough detail to read terrain height and material, separated by thin neutral dark gutters. Maximize image area, high resolution, each quadrant one strong simple terrain scene, no tiny extra insets, no text or labels anywhere. All panels share purple-grey weathered basalt geology and realistic restrained game-concept art quality. No characters, vehicles, buildings, machinery, HUD, diagrams or captions.
TOP LEFT: archived cold-zone proposal: a shadowed low-temperature basalt fissure with a broad nearby ice-covered plain, translucent blue ice coating broken low cliffs and accumulating along the fissure floor. Dark bare rock protrudes from naturally feathered ice edges, local frost fades into dry basalt outside the shaded pocket. This is a localized cold rift and ice sheet, NOT alpine snow mountains, not the later frost planet, no geysers or thermal springs.
TOP RIGHT: future red-furnace mountains and archived geothermal zone: broad charcoal volcanic slopes and naturally fractured dark lava crust; a few narrow orange-red molten seams trace a tectonic fissure and emerge downhill into cooling black lobes. A readable natural lava-tube/mineral-cave opening embedded in the cliff side, faint steam and coppery mineral stains. Not an entire red glowing ocean and no lava falling upward, vegetation retreats gradually away from hot rock.
BOTTOM LEFT: future mirror-crystal canyon: deep eroded purple-grey canyon with a continuous pale dry floor and dark mineral seams, large irregular silvery smoky crystal facets grow from the rock strata at selected fissures. Crystals are integrated mineral outcrops, not a field of identical glowing spikes. Local reflected sky glints echo canyon walls, background rock route remains legible, no constructed bridge or ruins.
BOTTOM RIGHT: future storm plateau and archived gravity-anomaly mineral belt: broad flat high-altitude basalt grass plateau cut by one deep fissure, muted sage ground, heavy indigo storm clouds and one distant branching lightning flash. Three irregular fractured BOULDERS float over the local fissure at staggered heights due to the documented anomaly; matching broken sockets and mineral veins in nearby rock establish their source. They are localized natural rocks, not square landscape tiles or entire levitating continents. Keep ground itself continuous, no rectangular cutouts, no patterned grid.
Across all four: geographical material transitions follow erosion, frost, heat or fractures, no square biome patches, no text, no snow mountains or dunes. This sheet is solely old-draft and future-terrain design for review, not a claim of implemented gameplay.
